verdicts.claim: 1.102 (2023-02-01): CesiumJS now defaults to a WebGL2 context; falls back to WebGL1; set requestWebgl1:true in ContextOptions to force WebGL1; requestWebgl2 deprecated in 1.101
verdicts.note: Fetched the raw file at unpkg.com/cesium@1.103.0/CHANGES.md. Under '### 1.102 - 2023-02-01': 'CesiumJS now defaults to using a WebGL2 context for rendering.' / 'WebGL1 is supported. If WebGL2 is not available, CesiumJS will automatically fall back to WebGL1.' / 'to request a WebGL 1 context, set `requestWebgl1` to `true` when providing `ContextOptions`'. Under '### 1.101 - 2023-01-02': '`ContextOptions.requestWebgl2` was deprecated in CesiumJS 1.101 and will be removed in 1.102.' Caveat: the current CHANGES.md (1.134 section) says WebGL2 is 'enabled by default since 1.101' linking PR 10894; Cesium's own changelog is internally inconsistent, and the 1.102 release note is the primary statement of the default switch.

verdicts.claim: Offline guide: imagery (api.cesium.com, dev.virtualearth.net), geocoder (api.cesium.com) and BaseLayerPicker are the external dependencies; configure baseLayer from another provider, geocoder:false, baseLayerPicker:false
verdicts.note: Guide: default imagery is 'Cesium ion global imagery through Bing Maps' loading from api.cesium.com and dev.virtualearth.net 'as well as several other tile servers that are subdomains of virtualearth.net'; Geocoder 'uses the Cesium ion API at api.cesium.com' -> pass geocoder: false; BaseLayerPicker -> pass baseLayerPicker: false or configure imageryProviderViewModels/terrainProviderViewModels. Example passes baseLayer: ImageryLayer.fromProviderAsync(TileMapServiceImageryProvider.fromUrl(buildModuleUrl('Assets/Textures/NaturalEarthII'))), baseLayerPicker: false, geocoder: false.

MVTDataProvider 'experimental' status: CHANGES.md 1.142 does not use the word experimental for MVTDataProvider (it uses it for EXT_mesh_polygon / 3DTILES_content_gltf_vector). The experimental marking comes from the ref doc (https://cesium.com/learn/cesiumjs/ref-doc/MVTDataProvider.html): 'This feature is not final and is subject to change without Cesium's standard deprecation policy.' Cite the ref doc, and note the documented entry point is MVTDataProvider.fromUrl(urlTemplate with {z}/{x}/{y}, { minZoom: 0, maxZoom: 14, extent, featureIdProperty }); no PMTiles/archive input is documented, so PMTiles-backed hydrography needs a tile server (e.g. Martin) or a custom Resource in front of it.

Draping: '1.144 drapes clamped vector polygons/polylines on terrain' is confirmed ('Added support for draping clamped vector tile polygons and polylines onto terrain, with screen-space-constant line width and per-feature styling via Cesium3DTileStyle', #13577/#13627). The pre-staged 1.145 section already contains a fix ('draped vector polylines rendering at twice their specified width' + antialiasing toggle scene.vectorProvider.antialias), so hands-on testing should use 1.145 when it ships on 2026-09-02.

WebGL2 default wording: keep '1.102' as the release that switched the default (1.101 only announced the change and deprecated requestWebgl2), but note that the 1.134 CHANGES entry ('Voxel rendering now requires a WebGL2 context, which is enabled by default since 1.101') contradicts this; cite the 1.102 release note as primary. The voxel requirement itself dates from 1.134 (2025-10-01).

OSM credit: do not rely on OpenStreetMapImageryProvider's default credit 'MapQuest, Open Street Map and contributors, CC-BY-SA' -- it is stale (ODbL since 2012). Pass credit: '© OpenStreetMap contributors' (and link to openstreetmap.org/copyright) per OSM attribution guidelines.

Bundle size: report gzip as ~1.73 MB and state the compressor (1,730,610 bytes with gzip -9; 1,735,163 with default level 6). The raw sizes 5,974,765 / 15,662,452 / 30,710 bytes are exact, and widgets.css lives at Build/Cesium/Widgets/widgets.css.

Cesium ion Community plan (open question closed): pricing page literally says 'Free (individual)'; eligible uses 'Non-commercial personal projects, or Exploratory commercial or government development, e.g., evaluating if Cesium ion will meet your needs, or Unfunded educational activities'; a paid account is required 'if your company currently makes more than $50K in annual gross revenues or has raised funds in excess of $50K'; 5 GB storage, 15 GB / month streaming, 1,000 Global Imagery sessions / month, 1,000 Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles root tiles / month. The logo rule is in the Cesium ion Terms of Service §2.2.3: 'making the Cesium ion logo prominently viewable to users' and 'the Cesium ion logo must be prominently displayed on the main application window of Your Application' (splash/about page acceptable only for mobile/VR). ToS §2.2.2 also forbids copying/storing/redistributing Cesium Data Output for offline use (only general-purpose client/proxy caching allowed) -- add this to the ion section. Pricing page lists Global Imagery as 'Bing Maps, Google Maps; Azure Maps as Technology Preview'; the 2028-06-30 Bing cutoff date was not verified in this pass.

WA DNR lidar licensing (open question closed as far as published text allows): the Washington Geological Survey 'Disclaimers and Citation Guidelines' page (https://www.dnr.wa.gov/programs-and-services/geology/publications-and-data/disclaimers-and-citation-guidelines) states: 'All of the materials we produce (publications, digital content, posters, videos) are free for you to use in any way you choose, for both commercial and non-commercial purposes, including modifying or adapting anything, as long as you cite us.' and gives a lidar citation template ('Washington Geological Survey, 2023, Olympics Wali 2022 project [lidar data]: originally contracted by Washington Dept. of Natural Resources. [accessed ..., at https://lidarportal.dnr.wa.gov]') plus a no-warranty disclaimer. Neither the portal (lidarportal.dnr.wa.gov) nor its help.html carries any license text. Replace 'public domain (third-party blog)' with 'free for commercial and non-commercial use with citation, per WGS Disclaimers and Citation Guidelines' and keep an attribution line in the app. Lidar Manager contact for rehosting confirmation: Abigail (Abby) Gleason, abigail.gleason@dnr.wa.gov, 360.902.1560 (Lidar Specialist: Guy McWethy, guy.mcwethy@dnr.wa.gov). The 'public domain' sentence attributed to the 2023 WA State Lidar Plan PDF could not be extracted from the PDF text.

MapTiler terrain-rgb-v2 (open question closed): official schema page https://docs.maptiler.com/schema-raster/terrain-rgb/ states tileset id 'terrain-rgb-v2', format 'webp', 'Min zoom: 0', 'Max zoom: 14', '30 m globally, 5 m in specific areas', vertical resolution '6 m'. Use max zoom 14; the '12' came from a stale snippet. Tile pattern follows the generic Tiles API 'GET https://api.maptiler.com/tiles/{tilesId}/{z}/{x}/{y}' -> https://api.maptiler.com/tiles/terrain-rgb-v2/{z}/{x}/{y}.webp?key=..., and a live probe of https://api.maptiler.com/tiles/terrain-rgb-v2/0/0/0.webp returned 403 'Missing key - Get your FREE key at https://cloud.maptiler.com/account/keys/' (endpoint exists; key mandatory; TileJSON at /tiles/terrain-rgb-v2/tiles.json?key=). Decoding formula is published on MapTiler's 2019 post (https://www.maptiler.com/news/2019/03/rgb-encoded-elevation-data-in-maptiler-cloud/): 'height = -10000 + ((R * 256 * 256 + G * 256 + B) * 0.1)'.

Esri attribution (open question partially closed): the 'Esri and data attribution' page is client-rendered (static HTML has no attribution text), so exact logo/format rules remain unconfirmed. Literal evidence available: ArcGIS Maps SDK for JavaScript licensing page requires displaying 'Powered by Esri' text and 'all data source provider names' in any app using ArcGIS services; the Static Basemap Tiles REST doc states 'Applications that use this service must display both basemap and data attribution', base URL https://static-map-tiles-api.arcgis.com/arcgis/rest/services/static-basemap-tiles-service/v1, tile path /{style}/static/tile/{level}/{row}/{column} (i.e. z/y/x order -- a Cesium UrlTemplateImageryProvider template must be .../{z}/{y}/{x} with tileWidth/tileHeight 512), 512x512 PNG, zoom 0-22, '2 million free then $0.15 per 1,000 tiles', and data-attribution metadata is served from each style's /static endpoint.

Viewer options: the research should not mention an imageryProvider option -- the current Viewer ConstructorOptions table has only baseLayer (ImageryLayer | false). An ion-free viewer therefore needs baseLayer: <ImageryLayer from UrlTemplateImageryProvider> (or false), geocoder: false, baseLayerPicker: false, and a non-ion terrainProvider/terrain; this matches the Offline Guide example.
